observations.result: 48 committed vectors: 1 expecting PASS, 47 expecting BLOCK
for every vector the two implementations produce the same verdict line and the same exit code
the two are written in different languages, with different JSON decoders and different signature libraries; neither was adjusted to make the other agree
the second implementation was built from the published specification; the one gap it hit, trust-anchor public keys omitted from the document, was recorded and closed by publishing them
both suites run on every change to this repository; the reference suite on ubuntu, windows and macos, the second implementation on ubuntu

omitted: the private system that produced the passport the vectors are derived from, and its signing keys

limitations: Both implementations come from this project. This is agreement between two implementations, not two parties checking each other.
Agreement covers the 48 published vectors. It says nothing about inputs outside them, and does not establish correctness in general.
Four declared refusal reasons are not reachable by mutating the published bytes and are therefore absent from the vectors; reaching them requires a differently signed record.
Passing the suite is not a statement that an implementation is safe to rely on.
